basis: ABS CPI as used in ../sharp_grid_reference/ (A009 there)
justification: ShARP's charge is in A$2024 and the campaign's costs are real June 2025 dollars; the factor is the June quarter 2025 index over the mean of the four 2024 quarters, the same one the dashboard's ShARP overlays use.

short_name: charge per MWh generated through ShARP's delivery factor
justification: ShARP prices a MWh of national delivered electricity; one MWh generated in the NEM delivers 0.7915 MWh on ShARP's own bridge, so the charge per MWh generated is 0.7915 of the charge per MWh delivered. This is the same per-MWh factor the common-basis cost conversion applies to every ShARP price.

short_name: capacity factor of the 2027-2030 new build mix
basis: Step Change CDP4 capacity and energy FY2026 to FY2030 (S004)
justification: The generation allowance is pooled across wind, solar and gas, so one per-MW charge needs one capacity factor. Added wind and solar energy (92 TWh) over added wind, solar and gas capacity (39 GW) gives the path's own mix; gas output falls over the span so its capacity counts with no energy.

short_name: battery discharge hours from the base chain of run 2026-09-22T22.46_sc5
justification: No published source gives NEM battery discharge per MW; that run's base 2030 period discharged 12.016 TWh from 14.59 GW of existing and committed batteries. Charging storage per MWh discharged is a convention, since a battery adds no net energy.
key: Discharge hours per MW per year

justification: ShARP applies the short-lead-time adjustment to growth installed in FY2030 and lets it expire after that year, so the adder enters the 2030 period's objective and is not carried forward as capital cost of the surviving build.
used_for: Temporal scope of the rush tranche

justification: The campaign already prices build rate in every period through ../build_rate_premium/, which stands in for ShARP's persistent bands; adding the first band would give ShARP's combined A$39.603218/MWh and raise both adders by 5.8 per cent.
